name: De Tomaso Pantera GT5-S
description:
The De Tomaso Pantera GT5-S is one of the most extreme iterations of the legendary mid-engined Italian-American sports car. Successor to the De Tomaso Mangusta, the Pantera is a two-door, mid-engine sports car first produced in 1971. The GT5-S variant, introduced in the 1980s, took the Pantera formula to new heights with dramatically widened bodywork, aggressive aerodynamic enhancements, and substantial performance upgrades.

This particular example has been professionally tuned with engine modifications providing a 15% power increase over stock, resulting in improved performance throughout the rev range while maintaining reliability. Designed by American car designer Tom Tjaarda, the GT5-S featured distinctive fender flares to accommodate much wider wheels and tires, a massive rear wing for improved high-speed stability, and NACA ducts for enhanced cooling.

The car is built on a steel chassis with a monocoque design, featuring retractable headlamps and aggressive styling that made it unmistakable on the road. Powered by Ford's legendary 5.7-liter Cleveland V8 engine, this tuned GT5-S offers thrilling performance with its lightweight construction and mid-engine balance. The Pantera GT5-S was an exclusive vehicle built only on request, with the last examples delivered in the early 1990s.
